main_text.p: ductum esse censerem, quam quia forte non satis esset virium aut audaciae in uno. Et cum quisque in se minimum haberet fiduciae, iuncto comite, augeretur cuiusque animus, omnisque metus pelleretur. Consortium quippe aliquod confert adiumentum atque solatium in periculo. Et levamen est in morte habere sodalem. Tumque socii atque comites inclamant, incitant, hortantur, ut cui inter pugnandum labitur animus, novo quasi celeusmate, erigatur. Quid quod ideo, secundum aut tertium comitem eligant, ne si forte vulnerati, aut in terram dilapsi, ab adversario trucidentur. Ne forte ultra sanguinis emissionem aut vulnera, licet non lethalia procedatur. Quæ, quid aliud indicant, quam multos duellatores esse meticulosos, iis animum plerum-

page.notes: The text is set in one column with no marginal notes. Paragraph breaks are hard to judge from the scan, so the page is given as one paragraph. The word "ple-" at the line end is hyphenated and continues as "plerum-" on the next page; the bottom "rum-" is the catchword. Long s is written as s throughout, including in "esset", "sodalem" and "si". The letter shapes in "fiduciae", "forte" and "ductum" were read as printed, and "Consortium" is taken from the long-s form on the scan. The watermark at the bottom right is a digitiser's mark and is left out.
